Tem 1.title: The Ground Fights For You
Tem 1.spine: You never chase anything. You make the ground expensive and let them come to you through it.
buys: A Restrain at range, and the gate to the rest of the column
Your free Draw Mana terrain now cuts
Spend Investiture to grow the terrain instead of recasting
A Reaction: punish anyone entering your ground
TIER 2. Grow the field as a free action; dice double
Allies attacking into your terrain add your Green
Your terrain no longer slows you
A mark to aim it all at
Weapon hits add vital damage per Insight
fight: Draw Mana on turn one. The zone lands before anyone closes.
Hold the far side of it. Let them wade; Thorn Field bills them per turn.
Spreading Roots to chase a retreat instead of chasing them yourself.
room: Primal Awareness means you are never Surprised outdoors. Say so.
You are the tracker. Lead with Survival and Perception.
Grasping Vines detains without hurting — a threat you can take back.
Tem 1.catch: Terrain only works if you place it early. Draw Mana costs an action, so a fight you enter at melee range is a fight this build spent badly.
Tem 1.next: Grasping Vines is the gate to the whole Territory column — Thorn Field and Spreading Roots both hang off it — and it tests Green (+4), your best casting number.

Tem 2.title: The Pack Closes
Tem 2.spine: You are worth more standing next to someone than standing alone. Everything here pays out when two of you hit the same target.
buys: Tracking advantage — and the gate to the column
Bonus damage per attacker on a shared target
Free advantage each round on the weakest enemy
Move the whole party without provoking, then hit harder
TIER 2. A Reaction warning for the pack; dice double
Force an enemy to move where you want it
The capstone: the pack acts as one
A mark the whole party can see
Weapon hits add vital damage per Insight
fight: Move adjacent to whatever a friend is already fighting. That is the whole build.
Pack Hunter for advantage; Coordinated Hunt pays per attacker on the target.
Scent the Weak tells you who is nearly down. Finish that one.
room: Survival and Perception are your best social tools — you read people like tracks.
You have no persuasion. Let Hannah talk; you stand where you can be seen.
Primal Awareness: no ambush outdoors ever surprises the party.
Tem 2.catch: This build does nothing alone. Every payoff needs an ally adjacent to the same enemy. If the party splits, you are a Scholar with a hammer.
Tem 2.next: Predator's Instinct needs Survival 2, so both ranks go there. It gates Scent the Weak and Coordinated Hunt — the entire Instinct column runs through it.

Tem 3.title: The Mark
Tem 3.spine: Pick one creature and make every hit on it worse than the last. Insight only ever goes up.
buys: A Restrain at range, and the gate to the Territory column
Your free Draw Mana terrain now cuts
Knowledge opens. Insight starts stacking
Your weapon becomes the payoff — vital damage per Insight
TIER 2. Insight builds itself every turn; dice double
Free vital damage on every hit
The finisher, priced in Insight
A kill rolls the count into the next target
The whole party rides your mark
fight: Studied Mark the biggest threat. You also read its HP and defenses.
Predatory Strike every round. Accumulate stacks Insight for free.
Cash out with Killing Blow; Death Mark carries the count onward.
room: Studied Mark works out of combat — it names the dangerous one before anyone speaks.
You are the tracker, not the talker. Lead with Survival and Perception.
Grasping Vines detains without hurting.
Tem 3.catch: Buy a heavy weapon first. Your Mace rolls Light Weaponry +3 — worse than your fists. Hammer 1d10 is the upgrade; the Axe is thrown, and fixes your ranged gap.
Tem 3.next: Grasping Vines is both a good pick and a required one — Thorn Field is gated behind it — and it tests Green (+4), your best casting number.

Hannah 1.title: What Follows Her
Hannah 1.spine: Something is leaning on you and you have stopped noticing. It gets easier to make people do things. That should worry you.
buys: Take an enemy's turn away and spend it yourself
Their spent focus feeds you
Spend Opportunity to read what they intend
Everyone near you finds obedience easier than resistance
TIER 2. Pull a thought straight out of a head; dice double
You stop being read in return
Their doubt is now a standing condition
A free action that makes closing on you unpleasant
The capstone: their reaction becomes yours
fight: Hollow Command the biggest threat — a wasted enemy turn beats damage you cannot deal.
Coercive Pressure is passive. Just stand where the enemies are.
Puppeteer at 10 turns their Reaction against them, once per round.
room: Deception is your top skill by level 6. Lead with it.
Extract Thought answers questions nobody agreed to answer.
Predatory Insight on an Opportunity: know what they want before you ask.
Hannah 1.catch: Black tests off Presence, not Intellect. Three attribute points into Presence take Black to +8 and your Investiture to 7 — and this tree spends Investiture constantly.
Hannah 1.next: Hollow Command is a root pick, so it needs nothing but the Black rank — and every Subjugation talent below hangs off it.

Hannah 2.title: The Room Is the Fight
Hannah 2.spine: You are a Law-Singer. Win the argument and the combat never starts — and when it does, you end it early.
buys: Deflect on demand for a character who has none
Fashion expertise, and advantage on your first face test
Pacify comes online; resisting you now costs focus
Free permanent advantage whenever you take a slow turn
TIER 2. Pacify them all and combat stops
Spend Opportunity to read the pattern and act on it
React to a failure and turn it into information
Turn their own claim against them
Cancel an enemy's Investiture outright
fight: Steadfast Challenge the loudest enemy. Disoriented, and disadvantage against you.
Calm Appeal pacifies what you Disoriented. Stack them up.
Peaceful Solution as a free action: all non-minions pacified, fight over.
room: This is where the build lives. Persuasion +6, Discipline +6 by level 10.
Well Dressed gives advantage on your first test in any scene. Dress for it.
False Premise lets you reject a claim as a Reaction — the Law-Singer's veto.
Hannah 2.catch: Peaceful Solution only ends a fight if every non-minion is pacified. That means Steadfast Challenge landing repeatedly, so Discipline 3 by level 6 is not optional.
Hannah 2.next: Withering Retort needs Discipline 2, so buy the rank now. It is deflect for a character with none, and the whole pacify line is gated behind it.

Hannah 3.title: The Omen-Caster
Hannah 3.spine: Your best skill is Blue, and Blue has no attack talents. Chaos tests Blue. One skill rank turns your strongest number into a weapon.
buys: A ranged attack at last, and it rolls your best skill
Two Omens a cast
A Reaction that makes an enemy reroll and take the worse result
+2 Cognitive and Spiritual — you are fragile
TIER 2. Detonate every Omen at once; dice double
Isolated, and vital damage off an Omen
See through walls; Investiture pays you back
Double dice of vital damage, paid in your own blood
Omen the room, then end it
fight: Entropy Strike the biggest threat. Spirit damage ignores armour entirely.
Spreading Omen to get a second one on. Never exceed your Omen cap.
Cascade Collapse detonates them all at once and Disorients the survivors.
room: Blue Attunement gives advantage on your next Cognitive test after Draw Mana.
Forewarned: call one character and one action each round. Free reaction if you are right.
Steadfast Challenge is still your best social lever.
Hannah 3.catch: Spirit and vital damage ignore deflect. That is the point: armour does nothing against you. But every Omen costs Investiture, and you only hold tier at once.
Hannah 3.next: Chaos needs Blue 2 and Black 2. You already have Blue 2 — so one skill rank opens the entire tree, and its opening attack rolls your strongest skill.

Soggy 1.title: The Surgeon
Soggy 1.spine: You will not out-damage anyone. Be the reason nobody dies.
buys: Real healing. The party has none
Field Medicine becomes a free action
An ally's success sets up the next ally's
Erudition reaches Spiritual skills; gates Collected
TIER 2. Fate opens; White reaches +5
+2 Cognitive and Spiritual
Revive the unconscious — or the newly dead
Healing scales off Lore as well
Your ground hands out temp HP every round
fight: Stay at the back. You have 11 HP and no armour.
Swift Healer makes Field Medicine free — heal and still take your action.
Draw Mana heals everyone in range for your tier. It is never a wasted turn.
room: Erudition re-slots two cognitive skills on a long rest with library access. Use it.
Medicine +6 by level 10 — you are the party's doctor out of combat too.
Moon-Pool Rites and Night-Work are your expertises. Lean on them.
Soggy 1.catch: Every step of the Surgeon line gates on Medicine ranks — Swift Healer needs 2, Resuscitation needs 3. Medicine 3 is impossible before level 6, so buy early.
Soggy 1.next: Nobody in this party can heal. You are the only candidate, and every step below gates on Medicine, so start buying it now.

Soggy 2.title: The Line Holds
Soggy 2.spine: You do not act. You make everyone else's action land better, and you never miss because you never roll.
buys: An ally's success raises the stakes for the next ally
The party moves as one body
A standing point everyone benefits from
Share your resolve against influence
TIER 2. Move the whole line without provoking; White reaches +5
Spend Opportunity to heal everyone near you
An anchor that holds the formation together
Bind an enemy to terms they must keep
You stop being moved or influenced
fight: Guiding Signal the target the party is about to focus. It raises their stakes.
Ordered Advance moves everyone at once — the whole line repositions free.
Draw Mana heals every ally in range. Do it whenever nobody needs a signal.
room: Terms of Accord binds an agreement mechanically. That is a Law-Singer's dream and it is yours.
Deduction +6 and Insight +6 by level 10 — you are the one who notices the lie.
You never roll White socially if you can help it; Willpower 0 is the weak spot.
Soggy 2.catch: Almost nothing here rolls, which is the point — White tests off Willpower and yours is 0. This build spends its whole career avoiding that die.
Soggy 2.next: Concordant Presence hangs off the Guiding Signal you already have, and it opens the entire Coordination column above it.

Soggy 3.title: The Ground Is Already Decided
Soggy 3.spine: You decide where the fight happens before it starts, and the enemy walks into it. No attack roll is ever made.
buys: An ally's success sets up the next — and buys the Green you need
Ally squares: +1 defenses, and Aid at 30 ft
The damage engine, and it makes no attack roll
See their turn, then slide a trap into their path
TIER 2. Your ground hands out temp HP; dice double
+2d8 and Disoriented on every trap
A Reaction that taxes them on every instance of damage
Link two squares: free Aid and free Reactive Strikes
Declare a prophecy; the whole board goes off at once
fight: Ordained Ground first — free action, and your allies want to stand on it.
Snare the square they must cross. It triggers on their turn, not yours.
Read the Threads, then move a Snare into where they are about to walk.
room: Read the Threads works on anyone — you learn what they mean to do next.
Awareness 6 by level 9 makes Insight and Perception your sharpest tools.
Ordained Ground extends Aid to 30 ft. Useful far outside a fight.
Soggy 3.catch: Snare adds your Awareness to its damage, so every attribute point pays three times — trap damage, max Investiture, and Spiritual defense. White never gets rolled at all.
Soggy 3.next: Fate needs White 2 (you have it) and Green 2 (you do not). Both ranks go to Green; Concordant Presence fills the level and hangs off your Guiding Signal.
